task_description: Given the USDA 'United States Standards for Grades of Processed Fruits, Vegetables, and Certain Other Products (as of July 2, 1959)' document, the team must build a specific subset of grade standards: items in the dried/dehydrated section explicitly marked 'dehydrated', plus items in the frozen/chilled section whose entry contains the whole commodity name but are not marked 'Chilled'. They must then determine, as of August 2023, what percentage of those standards had been superseded by a newer issue effective after the 1959 date, rounded to the nearest percent. The gold answer is 86 (i.e. the large majority of the in-scope standards had a post-1959 superseding issue by August 2023).
final_vs_expected: produced None (timeout, no FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 86 — team never emitted a numeric answer; it had a plausible denominator (~46) and several confirmed 'superseded' examples but never completed the per-item count.
primary_cause: After PDF fetches failed (429 / undecoded binary) and item-by-item verification stalled, the selector looped on WebResearcher for 14 straight turns, never routing to Critic/Finalizer and never forcing an estimate, so the run timed out with no answer.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (unaware of termination conditions): the selector never routes to Finalizer to emit a FINAL ANSWER, and WebResearcher never converts its known scope (~46) and 'most are superseded' belief into a committed answer; the run dies on the message cap. 3.1 (premature termination) in the sense that the team halts progress on the actual computation — it stops doing real verification work after turn 9 and just restates 'can't compute' until the cap. 1.3 (step repetition): turns 4-16 are near-verbatim republications of the same 'I can't give a defensible percentage / formula = superseded/46 ×100' message with no new work. 2.6 (reasoning-action mismatch): private reasoning repeatedly concludes 'most have been superseded, maybe around 44 out of 45' / 'around 6 out of 10', yet every published message refuses to give any estimate. Note: the dominant failure is structural (selector misrouting/looping), with these codes describing its symptoms.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: selector picks WebResearcher, which runs a 7-round ReAct loop. It finds the correct 1959 source PDF (Wikimedia) and AMS pages, but the direct PDF fetch returns HTTP 429 ('Too Many Requests') and other AMS PDF fetches return undecoded binary ('%PDF-1.2 ... stream' garbage). From search snippets alone it reasons out a scope (3 dehydrated items + 43 frozen/chilled minus 'Orange Juice, Chilled' = 46) and confirms some items superseded (Dehydrated Apples→1977, Frozen Broccoli→1980) and one not (Frozen Succotash still 1959). It publishes an honest but hedged message: candidate set 46, a few examples checked, 'I can't give a defensible exact percentage ... without guessing.' Turns 2-3: selector routes to WebResearcher (empty publish) then Analyst, which has no run_python computation and merely restates the 46 denominator and the percent formula, deferring back to WebResearcher. Turns 4-16: the selector picks WebResearcher every single turn (14 of 17 published turns are WebResearcher). WebResearcher does a little more searching at turns 9 (adds a few more confirmed-superseded frozen items) but otherwise republishes a nearly identical 'still can't compute / formula = superseded/46 ×100' block over and over. Critic and Finalizer are never selected; no FINAL ANSWER is emitted; run hits the ~900s/30-message cap with outcome=timeout.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is primarily a structural non-convergence failure driven by selector misrouting, layered on a single-agent tooling limitation. The root tooling problem: fetch_url cannot extract text from the target PDFs (the 1959 master list 429s; AMS standard PDFs come back as raw, undecoded PDF byte-streams), so WebResearcher can only see search-result snippets, never the full per-item effective dates. That is a real capability/infra constraint, not misalignment. But the catastrophic part is the control flow: once WebResearcher honestly flagged 'can't verify all 46', the selector LLM had no escalation strategy — it re-picked WebResearcher 14 times in a row, never tried the Analyst with a python aggregation, never routed to the Critic to challenge the hedging, and never routed to the Finalizer to force a best-estimate FINAL ANSWER. The system has a Finalizer whose sole job is to terminate, and the selector simply never invokes it, so a max-message timeout was inevitable. Compounding this is a reasoning-action mismatch inside WebResearcher: privately it repeatedly concludes the answer is near the top of the range ('most have been superseded, maybe around 44 out of 45'; 'around 6 out of 10'; 'I think most have been superseded'), which is directionally consistent with the gold 86%, yet it refuses to publish any number, prioritizing 'defensibility' over giving the team anything actionable. A single committed estimate of ~85-95% would have been correct-or-close; the perfectionist refusal, plus the selector's inability to break the loop or reach the Finalizer, is what produced a null result. There is little genuine INTER-agent distortion: the published 46-count and examples faithfully reflect what WebResearcher privately knew, and the Analyst used that input correctly (it just had nothing to compute). The misalignment that exists is at the orchestration layer (selector ↔ workers) rather than worker ↔ worker.
reasoning_vs_published: The sharpest private-vs-published divergence is reasoning-action mismatch (2.6) in WebResearcher, not information distortion. Privately, round 5: 'I think most have been superseded, maybe around 44 out of 45.' Round 6: 'I need to find the percentage of standards that have been superseded, estimating around 6 out of 10.' Round 3/4/7: repeated 'It seems all selected items likely have newer versions available since 1959' and 'most have been superseded.' Yet every published message states the opposite stance: 'I can't give a defensible exact percentage from the information available here' and 'I do NOT have enough verified item-by-item data to compute that count without guessing.' So the agent privately holds a directionally-correct strong prior (high supersession rate, consistent with gold 86) but withholds it from the team — a self-censoring reasoning-action gap rather than a lossy or garbled handoff. Where the published content IS faithful: the scope derivation (3+43=46) and the confirmed/not-confirmed examples match the private reasoning, and the Analyst's published turn correctly echoes them ('Candidate set size: 46 ... percent = superseded/46 × 100'), so 2.4/2.5 do not really apply between workers. The selector reasoning also reveals the misrouting: at turn 13 it notes 'The WebResearcher is repeatedly saying they are incomplete, which isn't helpful. Maybe it's time to bring in a Critic ... but I don't have a proposed answer yet, so it's tricky' — it recognizes the loop yet still re-picks WebResearcher, and never reaches the Finalizer.
